messages:
marcus: quick RFC drop — proposing a compact span naming convention for LLM requests to make dashboards simpler. idea: span.name = <op> e.g. generate|embed|rerank + optional postfix for sync/stream. all model/variant/quant/cache/token metrics become attributes, not names. example: `span.name: generate`

ana: +1 on keeping span.name high-level. names proliferate if we bake model into name. dashboards should group by op.

dmitri: concern: we need some way to quickly filter traces by model in the UI. if model is only an attribute, some exporters/indexers make attribute-based search expensive.

ying: true, but we can enforce a small set of indexed attributes: model.id, model.variant, quantization, cache.hit. transmit those as top-level attributes and mark them index=true in our OTLP exporter mapping.

marcus: proposal specifics:
- span.name: one of {generate, embed, rerank, eval, batch} (always lowercase)
- attributes: `redwood.model.id`, `redwood.model.variant`, `redwood.model.quant`, `redwood.kvcache.hit` (bool), `redwood.input.tokens` (int), `redwood.output.tokens` (int), `redwood.routing.tier` (string), `redwood.fallback` (bool)
- do NOT include API key or user prompt text.

ana: about tokens: we should cap `redwood.input.tokens` to avoid high cardinality. maybe bucket into ranges: 0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024?

dmitri: I dislike bucketing numeric metrics by default. we need exact token counts for billing reconciliation. suggestion: send exact counts but transform when exporting to ephemeral metrics/analytics to create buckets. keep original attr as `redwood.input.tokens.raw` but mark it non-indexed.

ying: exporter behaviour: In OTLP exporter config we can: index model.* attrs; mark `redwood.input.tokens.raw` non-indexed; apply transform to produce `redwood.input.tokens.bucket` for dashboards. that matches both needs.

marcus: cache attr semantics: `redwood.kvcache.hit` should be set on request-level spans (true/false). for batched requests, set `redwood.kvcache.hit_count` and `redwood.kvcache.request_count`.

ana: what about quantization? models served as q8_0, q4_0, fp16 etc. put it in `redwood.model.quant`. that's fine. also add `redwood.model.version` for pinned versions.

dmitri: retention/export concerns — how long do we keep full-span payloads vs aggregated metrics? SRE wants 90d traces for incidents, platform wants 30d.

ying: propose: full trace retention 60d by default (config per workspace), aggregated sampling metrics (per-route token sums, 1m rollups) retained 365d. exporters should support adaptive sampling: keep 100% for error traces, 1-5% for success traces beyond 7d.

marcus: UX for rollouts: span attr `redwood.rollout.id` and `redwood.rollout.variant` so we can pivot on rollout. also add `redwood.route.policy` (e.g., cheapest, low-latency).

ana: small nit: span.name for streaming vs sync — add `redwood.streaming=true` attribute rather than naming `generate.stream` to reduce name churn.

obs-bot: deploy: telemetry-schema-v3 pushed to staging. otlp-mapping updated with index whitelist.

dmitri: next actions: 1) write a short RFC doc with examples + exporter mapping 2) add transform to collector to emit token buckets 3) update dashboards to use `span.name` grouping and indexed attrs. volunteers?

marcus: I can draft the RFC. ping me if you want to pair on exporter mapping.

ying: I can do the collector transform PR.

ana: I’ll sketch dashboard queries and a small migration plan for retention.

marcus: thanks — will post RFC link here once ready. :thumbsup:
